metadata.name: Rupert Murdoch
metadata.description: Australian-born American media proprietor whose public positions combine market economics, national sovereignty, cultural integration and support for immigration.
metadata.scope: Public speeches, interviews and conduct from the 2008 Boyer Lectures to the September 2023 retirement announcement. Earlier interviews supply background only. Outlet editorials and employees’ positions are not automatically attributed to Murdoch. This is an interpreted assessment, not his own quiz submission or a claim about his positions after 2023.
metadata.role: Media proprietor; chairman of News Corporation, News Corp and Fox Corporation during the reference period

axes.brief: Supports representative electoral institutions, independent courts and an adversarial press; direct-democracy mechanisms remain inferred.
axes.counterEvidence: Leveson testimony is a self-interested account. Media ownership and political access complicate his democratic rhetoric; they do not establish support for military government. Constitutional delegation is assessed literally, not treated as unlimited power.

axes.brief: Defends press criticism and ordinary privacy while accepting some public-safety restrictions. Exact surveillance, preventive-policing and outbreak-access rules are inferred.
axes.counterEvidence: His call for weapon restrictions differs from many Fox commentators. Vaccination advocacy is not proof of mandatory vaccination. Hacking under his ownership challenges professed privacy standards; his denial is not independent exoneration.
